Subject: Private deployment questions: license minimum + audit trigger

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency numbers. We're spinning up the procurement review now and have a couple of open items we need clarified before we route the MSA and Order Form to legal:

1) License floor for on-prem / VPC private deployment: The order form references a "minimum committed capacity" but the MSA doesn't clearly define what constitutes a breach if usage dips below that. Our finance team needs to understand whether a usage shortfall can be cured by a credit or requires an early-termination fee. Please confirm options (credit, true-up invoice, or termination).

2) Audit / evidence trigger: We have an internal control that requires the right to validate data residency and operator access if we suspect non-compliance. Your MSA mentions "reasonable audit" but we need to know trigger mechanics (notice period, scope limits, snapshot procedures).

Attached are our initial procurement redlines and an Order Form worksheet. Can we get a response by EOD Friday so we can keep our timeline?

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Senior Procurement Manager
Canyon Clinics

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license minimum + audit trigger

Emma — thanks for sending this over and for the clear redlines. Quick answers up front:

• License floor shortfall: Our standard is to handle below-commit usage with a 30-day true-up invoice for consumption below the committed baseline. We only consider termination for material, sustained shortfalls (e.g., >60 days and >50% shortfall). We can add explicit language to the Order Form specifying the cure window and the credit/true-up mechanism instead of an automatic termination right.

• Audit / evidence trigger: We support a customer-initiated audit pathway with these guardrails: 30 days' notice, limited-scope (data residency & operator accounts only), on-site or secured remote snapshot access coordinated with Redwood compliance, and a mutually agreed redaction process for operator logs that reveal personal data unrelated to the audit. We can accept an exhibit that defines the exact evidence types (e.g., console audit log export, snapshot hash) and the frequency (one full audit per 12 months plus ad-hoc with cause).

I'll loop in David (Legal) and Lauren (Product Ops) for formal redline language. If you have a preferred wording for the curb/true-up, paste it and we can fold it into the Order Form.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Jones <emma.jones@canyonclinics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license minimum + audit trigger

Emma / Mina — looping legal in. Draft suggested edits below (included in the attached PDF as tracked changes):

1) License floor: Proposed clause for Order Form: "If Customer's measured monthly usage is below the Committed Minimum for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days, Customer will be invoiced for the shortfall based on Customer's then-applicable per-unit rate. If Customer remains below seventy-five percent (75%) of the Committed Minimum for sixty (60) consecutive days, Redwood may provide written notice to cure. If Customer does not cure within thirty (30) days after notice, Redwood may terminate the Order Form for convenience; termination shall not affect any accrued payment obligations."

2) Audit: Proposed exhibit (to be attached to MSA as Exhibit D): 
- Trigger: Customer may request an audit upon reasonable belief of non-compliance; Redwood may request a demonstration of cause in writing.
- Notice and timing: Customer will provide at least thirty (30) days' written notice.
- Scope: Limited to evidence of data residency, access logs for operator accounts, and configuration manifests.
- Execution: Audit executed remotely via secure snapshot at a mutually agreeable time; on-site allowed by exception with pre-approved scope and cost recovery for Redwood's reasonable travel/administrative costs.
- Confidentiality: Redwood personnel and third-party evaluators will be bound by an NDA; any customer-sensitive data found outside the audit scope will be redacted.

We also propose a compromise on cost recovery: Redwood will absorb first two (2) hours of remote audit coordination per request; any incremental hours will be invoiced at Redwood's standard professional services rate (with a cap to prevent friction).

I'll attach the tracked change PDF for your counsel. If Canyon is comfortable with the cure/true-up and the Exhibit D carveouts, we can convert to a clean redline and push to signature.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Responses_20260408.pdf (tracked changes)

Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license minimum + audit trigger

Thanks — that addresses most concerns. Two follow-ups from procurement/legal:

1) Can we get the license-floor cure language to explicitly say we can elect a credit instead of payment for shortfalls (finance prefers credit against next period vs. an immediate invoice). If you can add a sentence offering that optionality ("Customer may elect, within 15 days of invoice, to apply the shortfall amount as a credit against future invoices"), we can accept.

2) Audit Exhibit: two asks — (a) add a one-time "witness" option for an independent third-party (Canyon-approved) to validate cryptographic snapshot hashes locally during remote execution, and (b) define a 30-day maximum turnaround for Redwood to schedule the remote snapshot once notice is given (we understand exceptions for blackout windows).

If you can update the tracked PDF with these two small edits, procurement will clear, and legal will move the MSA + Order Form to signature. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emma
